paragraphs: Rav Mari, son of Rav Chisda.

He lived in the time of Rava, his brother-in-law. In [Kiddushin 32b](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.32b.2), Rava served drinks at his son’s wedding. Rav Papa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua stood when he offered them a cup. Rav Mari and Rav Pinchas, sons of Rav Chisda according to one reading, did not stand, and Rava took offense.

[Ketubot 61a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.61a.15) tells of two pious men, identified in one version as Rav Mari and Rav Pinchas, sons of Rav Chisda. One gave food earlier and the other later. Elijah spoke with the one who gave food earlier.[^1]

notes.text: The consulted Kiddushin text has the singular “son of Rav Chisda” next to Pinchas. The alternative in Ketubot explicitly calls both men sons of Rav Chisda.
